document_title: A trial court struck an AI transcript. Texas's top court weighs it
_note: Slide strings read off the render report's text nodes and each frame's own source line by build_copy.py.
caption:
A Montgomery County court struck a transcript made with AI. 18 months later the Supreme Court of Texas heard argument over it.

The case began as a wrongful termination suit, Courthouse News reports. The employer did not object to the software at the deposition. Weeks later it moved to strike. In April 2025 the trial court struck it because no certified shorthand reporter prepared it.

Justice Kyle Hawkins asked why the court should set aside "this efficient, cost-effective tool," Courthouse News reports. Justice Jane Bland asked where the court would find the assurance of a human being standing behind the transcribed product.

The court's orders through October 9th carry no ruling. A judge can already order a certified reporter's transcript for good cause. If the deposition's video is the check, what will count as good cause?

#MontgomeryCounty #TexasSupremeCourt #CourtReporters

S6.headline: The rule already has a check
S6.body: Rule 203.6(a) lets a written transcription of a recording be used like a stenographic deposition. A court may still require a certified reporter's transcript first, for good cause shown.
strings: The rule already has a check
Rule 203.6(a) lets a written transcription of a recording be used like a stenographic deposition. A court may still require a certified reporter's transcript first, for good cause shown.
A non-stenographic recording of an oral deposition, or a written transcription of all or part of such a recording, may be used to the same extent as a deposition taken by stenographic means.

However, the court, for good cause shown, may require that the party seeking to use a non-stenographic recording or written transcription first obtain a complete transcript of the deposition recording from a certified court reporter.

S7.headline: "Why are we here?"
S7.body: Eight of the nine justices heard the argument on October 6th, Courthouse News reports. The Chief Justice observed that paying a certified reporter or letting the depositions go ahead this way would have been cheaper. Then he asked it. Drawn to illustrate.

S8.headline: Who stands behind the page?
S8.body: Justice Bland asked where the court would find the assurance of a human being standing behind the transcribed product. Five of the employer's twenty minutes went to the Texas Deposition Reporters Association. Drawn to illustrate.

S9.headline: Argued. Not decided
S9.body: Justice Young named escape hatches, the recording itself and a judge's power to order a certified reporter. Courthouse News read the bench as inclined to allow it. The court's orders through October 9th carry no ruling in the case. Drawn to illustrate.
